evidence.contextAndScope: Linux ARM32, AArch64, RISC-V and x86 entry requirements, U-Boot image commands, memory placement, cache/MMU/interrupt state and diagnostic guidance in chapter19.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The article placed the AArch64 DTB within a same 512 MiB region as a current rule (kernel docs limit that note to pre-v4.2); stated booti supports zImage; asserted fixed 1,024-byte cmdline and first-4-GiB x86 identity mapping; described D-cache as off; claimed OpenSBI is always present; used an entry address and synthetic U-Boot call sequence as universal. Title/description scope also omitted RISC-V/x86 content.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Legacy protocol notes, current boot protocol and U-Boot command implementation were combined as a single architecture-independent rule. Rewrote each architecture section against Linux v6.12 primary docs and separated direct Image entry from EFI/application path.
evidence.evidence: Linux v6.12 AArch64 docs require x0=DTB, x1–x3=0, non-secure EL1/EL2, interrupts masked, MMU off, image cache clean to PoC, DTB aligned/size bound and initrd window. ARM docs define r2 boot data and DT-only r1. RISC-V docs define a0/a1 and satp=0. x86 docs define protocol-specific boot_params/entry requirements. U-Boot v2025.01 command docs define bootm/booti/bootz syntax. See primarySources.

evidence.decision: Corrected verified protocol errors, removed unverified behavior, pinned explanation to Linux v6.12 and U-Boot v2025.01 sources, and manually aligned title/description with the four architectures in scope. Slug/date/series/order/draft unchanged.
